notice: AI-assisted adversarial engineering review. This is not human scientific approval, production approval, or evidence of predictive validity.
reviewCriteria: The response preserves the direction supported by the cited endpoint.
The response remains neutral outside the studied scope or when an input is missing.
Magnitude is smaller when endpoint, setting, life stage, or geographic transfer is uncertain.
Severe penalties activate only at the exact severe physiological condition.
Correlated temperature, light, tide, cloud, and flow signals cannot stack.
No curve is treated as validated merely because its deterministic tests pass.

magnitudeRevisions.reason: Baited-trap capture in one estuary is an indirect angling proxy, so the former full moderate envelope was too assertive.
The very-cold evidence includes a confounded field comparison and cannot support a five-percent ordinary score penalty.
Progressive ration differences establish direction but not a direct conversion to catchability, so the cold penalty was reduced.
The local study is highly relevant, but its predictors explained only a small share of feeding variation; the response is now minor rather than moderate.
A controlled juvenile feeding response does not justify the former full moderate envelope for adult field catchability.
Two field stomach chronologies support timing direction but not a ten-percent peak-to-trough catchability swing.

curveReviews.adversarialFinding: Nocturnal baited-trap capture is directionally useful but is not hook-and-line catchability and came from a turbid estuary.
Exact timing is verified, but stomach fullness over one July day in one stream may reflect digestion as well as feeding.
Virginia tidal-river fish improve transferability, but controlled maximum ration is not field angling success.
The warm-side direction requires sustained acclimation and must not respond to a single warm afternoon.
The nighttime signal is limited to very cold winter experimental conditions and cannot define the ordinary seasonal diel curve.
Feeding at 3 C is supported, while the near-2 C field comparison is confounded and cannot establish a universal threshold.
Temperature anchors support continued cold feeding and directional suppression, but not a direct ration-to-score conversion.
Cooling-day direction is usable only with genuine 24-48 hour water-temperature history and adds no warming bonus.
The severe treatment supports a guarded penalty, but juvenile aquaculture stress activity cannot be interpreted as positive catchability.
Large treatment differences support the bounded shape, but 28 C is not labeled a universal NOVA field optimum.
One summer stream chronology supports only a minor relative early-evening signal.
A distinct peak is confirmed, but its interval is unavailable; any timed response would be invented.
Juvenile laboratory cessation anchors justify a severe cold guardrail, not a claim that field capture is impossible.
The exact chronic 35 C condition supports a guardrail, but the study does not identify a lower onset temperature.
Angler-trip success is directly relevant, but one lake fishery cannot establish the same radiation slope for every NOVA water.
The study is local and directionally relevant, but predictors explained only six percent of feeding variation and sampling covered May-June.
Outgoing tide covaried with time of day and requires a trustworthy local tidal prediction plus a joint cap.
Controlled adult feeding supports direction, but NTU and FNU optics are not interchangeable with suspended-sediment mass.
The oxygen anchors are biologically direct, but a station value may not represent the fish's depth or selected access point.
The hook-and-line endpoint is direct, but the Wisconsin lake effect needs prospective NOVA validation and cannot stack with radiation or cloud.
Juvenile controlled feeding supports a broad intermediate-temperature shape, not a precise adult field optimum.
Summer chronologies support a late-evening peak, but stomach contents are not angling success and the response depends on clear water.

comparisonCohort.selectionRationale: Local tidal-Potomac feeding evidence, hourly solar input, exact May-June and tidal-water gates, and reduced minor magnitude.
comparisonCohort.validationScope: Prospective targeted trips in tidal Potomac or comparable connected tidal reaches during May-June, stratified across morning, daylight, and overnight periods.

comparisonCohort.selectionRationale: Direct compulsory-creel catchability endpoint, hourly solar input, simple nonstacking light representation, and conservative bounded uplift.
comparisonCohort.validationScope: Prospective targeted trips on documented NOVA or upper-Potomac lake/reservoir walleye waters, stratified across dawn, day, and dusk.

externalDatasetReview.reason: This is the source that motivated the snakehead rule, not an independent validation dataset.
The release contains specimen health, date, and location data but no targeted angling effort or catch/no-catch outcome.
The volunteer diary records effort and zero-catch trips, but it concerns muskellunge and publishes pooled summaries rather than suitable row-level cohort data.
The page documents managed fisheries and survey summaries but does not provide timestamped targeted-trip outcomes.

observationContract.unitOfAnalysis: one completed targeted angling trip for one species and one continuous fishing interval
requiredPractices: Record zero-catch trips rather than collecting catches only.
Lock the model version, fixture hash, and analysis plan before a trip can enter confirmatory evaluation.
Record the actual named spot and start/end time supplied by the angler; do not freeze a forecast in the trip-entry flow.
Reconstruct environmental inputs from independently archived, time-indexed sources without using the catch outcome.
Keep targeted and incidental catches separate.
Exclude exact private coordinates from public outputs.
Never scrape or republish restricted third-party catch reports.
Keep ordinary private trip logs in the calibration store; never copy them automatically into the formal validation-observation store.

validationStages.purpose: Verify ranges, interpolation, gates, caps, missing inputs, and nonstacking behavior.
Collect effort-aware targeted trips, including explicit zero-catch trips, against a locked model version; environmental inputs are replayed from independent historical sources.
Compare candidate-v0.2.0 against the current score on waterbody and time holdouts.
A named human reviewer accepts sources, curves, metrics, uncertainty, and release scope.

draftProtocol.instrumentationPilot: The first 30 consented trips per species are for form, coverage, missingness, duplicate, and variance checks only; they cannot establish predictive validity.
draftProtocol.primaryOutcome: Target-species catch count per angler-hour, analyzed with logged angler-effort as an offset.
secondaryOutcomes: Explicit zero-catch rate by predeclared activity stratum.
Probability of at least one target catch per trip.
Calibration and discrimination of the candidate score versus the current baseline on held-out waters and dates.
draftProtocol.minimumCoverageBeforeConfirmatoryDesign: At least 30 consented trips per cohort species, at least 10 trips in each compared solar stratum, and at least three waters where the evidenced distribution permits it.
draftProtocol.holdoutRule: Declare whole-waterbody and future-date holdouts after the instrumentation pilot using exposure and missingness only, before viewing catches by score stratum.
defaultExclusions: Incidental rather than targeted catch records.
Trips shorter than 15 minutes or longer than seven days.
Species not evidenced at the selected BiteMap spot.
Duplicate trips or mechanically implausible effort/catch values.
Rows whose historical condition replay lacks a required candidate input.
draftProtocol.antiLeakage: Catch outcome, lure, notes, and user identity may not select or alter historical condition inputs.

requiredBeforeObservationCollection: A named human reviewer signs the draft protocol before any row is promoted from calibration to confirmatory evaluation.
Use the outcome-blinded instrumentation pilot to set a precision- or power-based confirmatory sample size.
Declare exact waterbody and future-date holdouts before viewing held-out outcomes.
Declare the minimum held-out improvement and maximum calibration regression allowed.

humanApprovalGate.note: Must remain false until a named reviewer signs the source passages, curve choices, preregistration, and held-out results.
